Print and convert the representation of a context tree

Source: R/draw_print.R
print.mixvlmc_draw.Rd

draw() returns an object of class mixvlmc_draw that contains the text or LaTeX representation of a context tree. These functions print it and convert it to a character vector.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mixvlmc_draw'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mixvlmc_draw'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mixvlmc_draw'
as.character(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a representation of a context tree produced by draw().

...

additional arguments (not used).

Value

print() returns its argument (invisibly), format() and as.character() return the representation as a character vector, one string per line.

Details

print() writes the representation, one line after another. It is called automatically when the result of draw() is not assigned to a variable, for instance when draw(model) is called in the console.

In a knitr document (R Markdown, Quarto, ...), the result of draw() is printed as standard R output, except for a LaTeX representation (format = "latex") in a document that produces LaTeX (e.g. a PDF output). In this case, the LaTeX code is included as is in the document and the forest LaTeX package is loaded automatically at the end of its preamble (with the AtEndPreamble command of the etoolbox package), so that the tree is rendered. A document can also load forest in its preamble, possibly with options: it is then not loaded a second time.

See also

draw()

Examples

set.seed(0)
rdts <- sample(c(0, 1), 100, replace = TRUE)
ctree <- ctx_tree(rdts, min_size = 10, max_depth = 2)
tree_repr <- draw(ctree)
print(tree_repr)
#> ▪
#> ├─ 0
#> │  ├─ 0
#> │  └─ 1
#> └─ 1
#>    ├─ 0
#>    └─ 1
as.character(draw(ctree, "latex"))
#> [1] "\\begin{forest}"        "[\\textbf{$\\epsilon$}" "[\\textbf{0}"          
#> [4] "[\\textbf{0}]"          "[\\textbf{1}]]"         "[\\textbf{1}"          
#> [7] "[\\textbf{0}]"          "[\\textbf{1}]]]"        "\\end{forest}"
